title: Georgia's 1st Congressional District Election, 2026
description: Georgia's 1st Congressional District, anchored by Savannah and the coastal region, is an open seat after Republican incumbent Buddy Carter chose to run for U.S. Senate rather than seek re-election. The Republican primary on May 19, 2026 was won by Jim Kingston, an insurance salesman and son of former Rep. Jack Kingston, who secured the nomination outright with 52.7% of the vote in a crowded field. On the Democratic side, a runoff on June 16, 2026 between military veteran Joyce Marie Griggs and political strategist Amanda Hollowell was projected for Griggs, making her the Democratic nominee. The district leans Republican (Carter won 62% in 2024), but the open-seat dynamic and coastal demographics make it a race to watch.

candidates.name: Jim Kingston
candidates.summary: Jim Kingston is an insurance salesman and the son of former U.S. Representative Jack Kingston (GA-01, 1993–2015). He won the Republican primary on May 19, 2026 with 52.7% of the vote, avoiding a runoff in a seven-candidate field. Kingston's campaign emphasized border security, energy independence, and support for the Trump agenda, earning endorsements from Donald Trump, Ted Cruz, Mike Johnson, and the Club for Growth.

candidates.name: Joyce Marie Griggs
candidates.summary: Joyce Marie Griggs is a military veteran and community activist making her fifth consecutive run for Georgia's 1st Congressional District (2018, 2020, 2022, 2024, 2026). She advanced from the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary to a June 16 runoff against Amanda Hollowell, and was projected the winner of that runoff, securing the Democratic nomination. Griggs campaigns on veterans' affairs, healthcare access, and coastal economic development.

forecast.rationale: No public polling exists in the race data, which limits confidence. However, district fundamentals are strongly Republican-leaning: outgoing GOP incumbent Buddy Carter won 62% in 2024. In the open-seat contest, Jim Kingston (R) brings strong assets — outright primary win at 52.7% in a seven-candidate field, the well-known Kingston family name, and endorsements from Donald Trump, Ted Cruz, and the Club for Growth. On the Democratic side, Joyce Marie Griggs was projected the winner of the June 16 runoff but is a five-time candidate who has not previously prevailed in this district. Without polling or fundraising data showing a shift from the district's Republican baseline, Republicans remain clear favorites. The open-seat dynamic and lack of polling prevent a 'safe' rating, but the Republican advantage is evident.
